findings.title: Disabled-org wrapper on the original IDP skips needed login-cache invalidation
findings.body:
`update()` gets `idpById` through `getById()`, which returns the organization-aware wrapper. That wrapper's `isEnabled()` returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled. So for an IDP of a disabled org, `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` is false even though the DB row (what the JPA `getForLogin` query uses) is enabled, and the IDP id is in the cached login list.

If an admin then sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true or BROKER_PUBLIC=false, the updated model also fails the predicate. The first early-return fires and the login caches are not invalidated. Only `isEnabled()` is re-checked when the cached list is read, so once the org is re-enabled the cached `ORG_ONLY`/`ALL` lists still contain an IDP that is hidden, link-only or non-public. It is then shown on the login page.

The predicate for the original state should be evaluated against the raw stored model (e.g. `idpDelegate.getById`), not the org-aware wrapper.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", so created IDPs are never cleaned up
findings.body:
`getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` binds the cleanup to an IDP whose alias is literally "alias". It does not refer to the `idp-alias-N` providers created here. The same mistake is at line 425.

The 21 IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` therefore leak into later tests in the realm. That can skew counts and assertions in tests that run afterwards, such as the login-list sizes and `testCacheIDPByOrg`. Use the actual alias variable in the cleanup.
